# Braze

> Rewrite the rules of customer engagement with AI
> From cross-channel messaging and journey orchestration to Al-powered decisioning and optimization, Braze is a customer engagement platform that empowers brands to Be Absolutely Engaging.™

# Pages

- [Braze Learning Resource](https://www.braze.com/braze-learning-resource)
- [Home](https://www.braze.com/): Power customer-centric interactions between consumers and brands in real-time.
- [Value of Braze](https://www.braze.com/value-of-braze): All your channels, data, and experiences—all connected on one platform. Brands across the globe are using Braze to drive value and be Absolutely Engaging.™
- [The Braze Platform](https://www.braze.com/product): Discover how Braze works, the ultimate customer engagement platform. Unify data, personalize journeys, and optimize campaigns with AI-powered insights.
- [Get Started](https://www.braze.com/get-started): Join brands who are taking customer engagement to the next level. See how Braze can help increase lifetime value, brand loyalty, and simplify your tech stack.
- [About](https://www.braze.com/company)
- [Partners](https://www.braze.com/partners): Join the Braze Partner Program to drive customer engagement through partnerships. Enhance marketing efforts and business outcomes with tailored solutions.

## Product

- [Trust at Braze](https://www.braze.com/product/trust)
- [BrazeAI™ Agents](https://www.braze.com/product/ai-agents): Boost efficiency and personalization with BrazeAI™ Agents. Automate tasks, adapt in real time, and deliver meaningful engagement across every channel.
- [LINE](https://www.braze.com/product/line): Create stronger connections with LINE for your mobile-first customers in Japan and other parts of Asia, like Thailand, Taiwan, and Indonesia.
- [Product Overview](https://www.braze.com/product/overview): The only customer engagement platform you need. Braze helps marketers produce their best, most engaging experiences to help build customer relationships.
- [In-app Messaging Platform (SEO)](https://www.braze.com/product/mobile-app-messaging/in-app-messaging-platform): Power your app with an in-app messaging platform that drives engagement, retention, and conversions. Build seamless, personalized experiences with Braze.
- [BrazeAI™ Decisioning Studio](https://www.braze.com/product/brazeai-decisioning-studio): Deliver 1:1 personalization with BrazeAI Decisioning Studio™. Use all your first-party data to maximize impact and create experiences unique to every customer.

- [BrazeAI™](https://www.braze.com/product/brazeai): Unlock the power of AI with Braze. Create personalized customer journeys and automate marketing with AI-driven insights.
- [Omnichannel Marketing Platform (SEO)](https://www.braze.com/product/cross-channel-messaging/omnichannel-marketing-platform): Find out how omnichannel marketing platforms support personalized, consistent customer journeys—and why Braze is built for the job.
- [WhatsApp](https://www.braze.com/product/whatsapp): Unlock the power of WhatsApp marketing automation to create dynamic conversations and maximize your marketing ROI with Braze.
- [Braze Content Cards](https://www.braze.com/product/content-cards): Enhance customer engagement with Braze Content Cards™. Deliver personalized in-app messages with ease for seamless user experiences.
- [Braze Email](https://www.braze.com/product/email): Deliver personalized, dynamic emails that drive revenue. Enhance your marketing campaigns with Braze email marketing platform.
- [Braze SMS](https://www.braze.com/product/sms): Enhance SMS customer engagement with Braze. Integrate SMS into your strategy and reach users with 98% open rates via impactful text message campaigns.
- [Feature Flags](https://www.braze.com/product/feature-flags): Leverage Braze Feature Flags for feature management, A/B testing, and personalized customer engagement. Safely roll out new features with targeted control.
- [Reporting & Analytics](https://www.braze.com/product/reporting-analytics): Uncover insights, analyze performance, and find winning strategies across the customer journey. Contact us and learn about Braze Reporting and Analytics today!
- [Journey Orchestration](https://www.braze.com/product/journey-orchestration): Orchestrate memorable customer journeys that deliver the cohesive, responsive, and personalized experiences your customers crave with Braze Canvas.
- [Mobile App Messaging](https://www.braze.com/product/mobile-app-messaging): Coordinate personalized, contextually relevant mobile messages from a centralized mobile app marketing platform. Discover what Braze can do for you.
- [Web Messaging](https://www.braze.com/product/web-messaging): Drive engagement on your website by tailoring web messaging to visitor’s preferences, attributes, and behaviors. Convert them to customers with Braze today!
- [Media Audience Sync](https://www.braze.com/product/audience-sync): Leverage first-party data with Braze Audience Sync to enhance ad targeting, reduce spend waste, and boost conversions across channels.
- [Cross-channel Messaging](https://www.braze.com/product/cross-channel-messaging): Consolidate your messaging mix with a powerful cross channel marketing platform. Meet customers where they are through responsive, cross-channel experiences with Braze.
- [Braze Data Platform](https://www.braze.com/product/braze-data-platform): Harness the Braze Data Platform to manage and integrate first-party data. Enable data-driven marketing and customer engagement strategies with AI insights.

## Frequently Asked Questions

[What are BrazeAI™ Agents?](https://www.braze.com/product/ai-agents): BrazeAI™ Agents are autonomous AI assistants built into the Braze platform that help marketers work faster and smarter. They are highly configurable and can be deployed across the Braze platform, using your customers’ data and real-time context to automate tasks, personalize campaigns at scale, and help improve results across channels like email, push, in-app, and more.

[What types of agents does Braze offer?](https://www.braze.com/product/ai-agents): Braze offers three complementary types of agents. Marketers can easily build agents with Operator for common marketing tasks, like content generation and feedback analysis. Custom agents are built in the BrazeAI Agent Console™, and let you design task-specific, LLM-powered assistants that plug in directly in your Braze workflows. AI decisioning agents, available through BrazeAI Decisioning Studio™, make decisions at the individual customer level to optimize any business KPI. These agents can personalize channel, offer, message, creative, timing, frequency and more. They autonomously experiment and continuously learn from every customer interaction.

[How does the BrazeAI Agent Console™ work?](https://www.braze.com/product/ai-agents): Agent Console is an intuitive dashboard where marketers can create and manage custom agents without coding. You define the task, choose an AI model, and provide instructions (in the form of a prompt) for the agent. Agents are then invoked in either Catalogs or Canvases, to enrich data or personalize experiences, respectively. Currently, we are seeing customers use BrazeAI™ Agents to score leads, translate and localize content, and adapt communications based on customer behavior.

[How are custom agents different from conventional marketing automation?](https://www.braze.com/product/ai-agents): While traditional marketing automation runs on fixed rules and workflows defined in advance, custom agents bring AI models directly into Braze to generate outputs and route customers dynamically through Canvases. Instead of just following if/then logic, agents can enrich data, personalize content, and adapt to customer behavior in real time, giving marketers more flexibility and intelligence than conventional automation alone.

[What are common use cases for BrazeAI™ Agents?](https://www.braze.com/product/ai-agents): Brands can use BrazeAI™ Agents to tackle a range of marketing challenges, from driving conversions with personalized recommendations to reducing churn through timely offers, while also improving efficiency with tasks like scaling localization, enriching customer profiles, and automating campaign QA checks. Because agents can be shaped to fit each brand’s needs, they make it possible to scale everyday tasks and complex personalization in ways never before possible with Braze.

[Which AI models power BrazeAI™ Agents?](https://www.braze.com/product/ai-agents): BrazeAI™ Agents support leading large language models from providers like OpenAI, Anthropic, AWS, Microsoft Foundry, Databricks, and Google Gemini, giving marketers flexibility to choose their preferred LLM. AI decisioning agents rely on reinforcement learning, a type of AI best-fit for marketing personalization that optimizes customer and business value. With the Braze Model Context Protocol (MCP), you can also securely connect external AI tools to your Braze data for more advanced use cases.

[What is the difference between BrazeAI Decisioning Studio™ Go and BrazeAI Decisioning Studio™ Pro?](https://www.braze.com/product/ai-agents): BrazeAI Decisioning Studio™ Pro puts full-strength 1:1 decisioning behind your highest-stakes journeys. BrazeAI Decisioning Studio™ Go brings 1:1 decisioning to every journey, self-serve.

[What learning and development benefit opportunities does Braze offer to employees?](https://www.braze.com/company/careers/how-we-hire): We have many different learning and development initiatives and programs in place to ensure that employees can boost their skills and advance their careers, including our global learning stipend—check out the benefits section below for more details.

[Does Braze use AI in the recruitment process?](https://www.braze.com/company/careers/how-we-hire): At Braze, we’re committed to a fair and transparent candidate experience. To help our recruitment teams focus on what matters most — the person behind each application — we use AI-assisted tools at certain stages of our recruitment process. This includes using AI to analyze the experience, skills and qualifications in your application materials to help with screening and prioritizing candidates. Such screening may amount to a form of solely automated decision-making. We also use AI for administrative support, like scheduling and recording interviews and summarizing interview notes. Our recruiting teams remain responsible for all hiring decisions and are involved throughout the process. Depending on where you are located, you may have the right to request further information about how AI is used in our recruitment process, to opt out of AI-assisted review, to request a manual review of any decision made or to contest a decision. Please contact us at talentdata.privacy@braze.com for any requests or questions.

[How do I know if a Braze recruiter is real?](https://www.braze.com/company/careers/how-we-hire): Braze is aware of fraudulent recruitment activity in which bad actors may impersonate Braze recruiters and employees to deceive job seekers. These schemes are designed to obtain personal information or money, and are not affiliated with Braze in any way. BRAZE WILL NEVER Initiate contact via WhatsApp, Telegram, text message, or unsolicited phone calls as part of a recruiting process. Request payment, gift cards, banking details, or sensitive personal information (e.g. Social Security numbers or government IDs) during the interview process. Only once you receive and accept a job offer, you'll get requests for ID and personal details. For certain roles, you may be asked to verify your identity during the interview process, but that will specifically be requested through our Applicant Tracking System, Greenhouse. Ask you to purchase equipment or make any upfront payments. Contact you from a personal email address — all legitimate Braze recruiter communications come from a @braze.com email address. Use Crypto Currency to transact in forms of payment or purchases KNOWN FRAUD TACTICS Fake LinkedIn profiles WhatsApp outreach Telegram outreach Unsolicited texts & calls Fake Braze Website While you'll find our roles posted on many platforms (e.g., LinkedIn, Glassdoor, Indeed, etc.), you'll always be able to verify the legitimacy of Braze roles on our official careers website. If you believe you have been targeted by recruitment fraud, please report it to talentfraud@braze.com.

[Who is Braze built for?](https://www.braze.com/pricing): Braze supports companies at every stage of growth including startups launching their first engagement programs, to scaling companies meeting expansive growth, to large global enterprises looking for the leading customer engagement platform.

[What will my contract with Braze look like?](https://www.braze.com/pricing): Your Braze contract will be comprised of a Platform Edition tailored to your business needs, Monthly Active Users and Profiles, an allotment of Action Credits to power messaging and AI features, and CX Services to support your use of the platform. We also offer a variety of add-on SKUs across our Braze Data Platform and BrazeAI™ product suite so you can customize your contract and unlock other valuable features within Braze.

[What is a Monthly Active User? What is a Profile? Why are they important?](https://www.braze.com/pricing): A Monthly Active User (MAU) is any unique person who records a session on your Braze-connected app or website during a calendar month. You decide who counts: you can track every visitor if you value anonymous traffic, or limit tracking to only logged-in users. A Profile is the digital record of that person. It stores the user traits and behaviors that allow you to send truly personalized messages. Because your total user base is typically larger than your active monthly audience, every MAU in your plan includes a large allotment of User Profiles. This allows you to store data and re-engage customers with the right message, even if they haven't visited your app or website in a while.

[What products and channels does Action Credits give me access to?](https://www.braze.com/pricing): Braze Action Credits unlock the flexible use of any of the following features throughout your contract: Email, SMS/MMS, RCS, WhatsApp, LINE, KakaoTalk, Content Cards, Banners, Message Archiving, Audience Sync, Webhooks, BrazeAI Agent Console™, and BrazeAI Decisioning Studio™ Go. New and exciting features may be added to Action Credits in the future, giving you instant access to use them upon release.

[How do Action Credits work?](https://www.braze.com/pricing): Think of Action Credits as a single, flexible currency for your Braze account. Instead of purchasing fixed quantities for individual products, you buy one pool of credits as part of your contract. You can then use those credits across different channels and features based on your engagement strategy. Each action consumes a different number of credits—for example, sending an SMS may cost 1 credit, while a WhatsApp message may cost 5. Because all usage draws from the same pool, you can easily shift spend (e.g., from Email to Agent Console) without needing to contract a new product. Credits give you the flexibility to adapt your strategy as your customer needs change and your business strategy evolves.

[How will I be able to track my usage?](https://www.braze.com/pricing): Braze has comprehensive reporting and billing dashboards to help you monitor performance throughout your contract.

[What kind of support will I get?](https://www.braze.com/pricing): Braze offers a variety of Support and Service plans to fit customer needs including 24x7x365 Customer support for the world's leading brands. From initial implementation to long-term strategy, we deliver support and partnership, wherever you need it, when you need it. Check out our Support & Services to learn more: https://www.braze.com/customer-support-services

[Does Braze offer a free plan?](https://www.braze.com/pricing): Braze does not offer a free plan at this time. Companies can still explore the platform through trials, startup programs, and other tailored entry plans. Speak to your account manager or contact us for more details.

[What is the difference between BrazeAI Decisioning Studio™ Go and BrazeAI Decisioning Studio™ Pro?](https://www.braze.com/product/brazeai-decisioning-studio): BrazeAI Decisioning Studio™ Pro puts full-strength 1:1 decisioning behind your highest-stakes journeys. BrazeAI Decisioning Studio™ Go brings 1:1 decisioning to every journey, self-serve.

[What is the Braze Creative Studio?](https://www.braze.com/product/creative-studio): The Creative Studio is a built-in hub for creative tools designed to help you move from idea to execution faster. It serves as a single, centralized place for your media library, templates, content blocks, brand guidelines, calendar, and dynamic content feeds. The Creative Studio is designed to be flexible, so you can pull in creative assets and content from a wide variety of sources and only use the specific features you need.

[How do the Figma and Canva integrations work?](https://www.braze.com/product/creative-studio): These integrations bridge the gap between design and delivery by connecting your creative tools directly to Braze. With the Figma integration, you can send designs to your Braze Media Library in minutes. The Canva integration lets you sync finished visuals and full emails to your Media Library in seconds. Both integrations ensure your marketing team is always working with the latest approved assets—no manual downloads, re-uploads, or developer tickets required.

[How does the Creative Studio speed up creative execution?](https://www.braze.com/product/creative-studio): The Creative Studio eliminates the "asset wrangling" bottleneck by streamlining the path from design to deployment. Instead of manual handoffs, a designer can update a banner in Figma or Canva and sync it directly to the Media Library, ensuring the latest creative is ready for use without any reworks. Marketing managers can then make quick brand updates to cross-channel templates and content blocks simultaneously, accelerating production for the entire team. The Creative Studio also provides a single place to manage connected content, catalogs, and promotion codes, ensuring that enriching campaigns with dynamic content is seamless and accurate.

[What makes Braze the best option for startups and small teams?](https://www.braze.com/braze-for-startups): Braze works well for startups because it delivers enterprise-level customer engagement in a platform that is easy for small teams to use. Braze lets you launch campaigns fast, personalize with real-time data, and drive ROI without adding complexity, ideal for lean marketing teams moving quickly.

[What role does BrazeAI™ play in cross-channel messaging?](https://www.braze.com/product/cross-channel-messaging): BrazeAI™ assists in creating and personalizing content, generating copy and creative, and determining the best channel and timing for each customer interaction.

[What is cross-channel personalization with email platforms?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/cross-channel-personalization-email-platforms): Cross-channel personalization with email platforms means using a unified marketing platform to deliver coordinated and individually relevant messages across email, SMS, push notifications, in-app messaging, and other channels. Rather than managing each channel separately, a single platform shares customer data and behavioral signals across every touchpoint to personalize each interaction in context.

[Why should brands consolidate marketing channels onto one platform?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/cross-channel-personalization-email-platforms): Brands should consolidate marketing channels onto one platform because separate tools create disconnected customer profiles, duplicated effort, inconsistent experiences, and double-counted attribution. A single platform with a shared customer profile means every channel draws from the same behavioral data, producing more reliable measurement and a stronger foundation for AI-powered personalization.

[What is the difference between cross-channel and omnichannel personalization?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/cross-channel-personalization-email-platforms): Cross-channel personalization coordinates messaging across digital channels, such as email, SMS, push, and in-app, using shared customer data so each interaction informs the next. Omnichannel personalization extends that vision to every touchpoint a brand has with a customer, including physical stores and customer service, making it a broader but harder-to-execute goal.

[How does email fit into a cross-channel personalization strategy?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/cross-channel-personalization-email-platforms): Email has the widest addressable reach of any owned channel, supports rich and detailed content formats, and delivers strong ROI across the customer lifecycle. Combined with push notifications, SMS, and in-app messaging, each added channel extends what email alone can achieve.

[What is channel consolidation marketing?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/cross-channel-personalization-email-platforms): Channel consolidation marketing is the process of moving from separate point solutions for each channel onto a single platform with a shared customer profile. The journey typically runs from email-only ESPs through email and SMS platforms to full cross-channel engagement platforms, where every channel draws from the same data in real time.

[What is real-time marketing?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/real-time-marketing): Real-time marketing is responding to a customer, a moment, or an event as it happens, rather than on a campaign calendar. It can mean reacting to a trend or live event that many people are following, or answering something an individual customer just did, like leaving items in a cart or reaching a loyalty milestone.

[What is an example of real-time marketing?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/real-time-marketing): A price-drop alert is a common example. When the price falls on an item a customer has saved or viewed, an email or push notification goes out showing the old and new price. It arrives at the moment the price changes, which is exactly when the customer’s reason for waiting disappears.

[What is the difference between real-time marketing and trend-jacking?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/real-time-marketing): Trend-jacking is one type of real-time marketing. It means a brand joins a trend, news story, or cultural moment while people are talking about it. Real-time marketing is broader. It also includes messages triggered by an individual customer’s actions, such as a browse, purchase, or a change in location, sent while that action still matters.

[What data does real-time marketing require?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/real-time-marketing): Real-time marketing needs customer events that stream in as they happen and segments that refresh as that data changes. Messages should trigger directly off those events, with frequency caps and quiet hours controlling how often and when they send. If data arrives in overnight batches, messages end up responding to yesterday’s behavior.

[Is real-time marketing only for social media?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/real-time-marketing): No. Trend response often happens on social media, but real-time marketing also runs on email, push notifications, SMS, and in-app messages. That’s where customer-level real-time marketing usually happens, responding to what one customer just did, like abandoning a cart or arriving near a store.

[What is eCommerce customer experience?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/ecommerce-customer-experience): eCommerce customer experience (CX) is the sum of every interaction a customer has with an online store, from how they discover a product through checkout, delivery, support, and the decision to buy again. It spans marketing, merchandising, eCommerce, fulfillment, and support functions, including the post-checkout window when order status and returns shape whether a customer comes back.

[How do you improve eCommerce customer experience?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/ecommerce-customer-experience): Start with the changes that bring the largest benefit for the least effort. Answer your most-asked support question, send order status updates before customers ask for them, and recover carts with their contents. Then, surface your returns policy before checkout, stop messages that contradict, use back-in-stock alerts, time reorder requests, and personalize.

[What metrics measure eCommerce customer experience?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/ecommerce-customer-experience): eCommerce customer experience is measured with three types of metrics. Outcome measures, like repeat purchase rate and revenue per customer, show whether the business is better off. Behavioral measures, like support contact rate, show what customers do. Survey scores like CSAT and NPS help explain why, but only a holdout group shows whether a change is successful.

[Which part of the eCommerce experience has the biggest effect on repeat purchase?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/ecommerce-customer-experience): The return or reorder decision tends to have the most direct effect on repeat purchase, and the delivery window often shapes that decision. An easy return, order updates that arrive without the customer asking, and a reorder message timed to when the product might need a replacement all make a customer more likely to buy again.

[Is eCommerce customer experience the same as eCommerce personalization?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/ecommerce-customer-experience): No, eCommerce personalization is one lever inside the customer experience, deciding which product, offer, or message each customer sees. Customer experience more broad and encompasses everything from site search and checkout to delivery, returns, and support, including aspects that messaging can’t influence, such as how quickly a refund arrives or whether a package is delivered on time.

[What is the best SMS marketing platform?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/best-sms-marketing-platforms): The right platform depends on your company's size, growth stage, and send volumes. For enterprise and high-volume consumer brands, consider Braze, Attentive, or Agentforce Marketing. For mid-market and growing brands, consider Klaviyo, MoEngage, or Iterable. Small businesses sending scheduled promotions to smaller lists can be well served by a simpler, dedicated SMS tool.

[What should an enterprise look for in an SMS marketing platform?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/best-sms-marketing-platforms): Enterprises should look for consent records they can rely on, number registration handled for them, throughput that suits large sends, documented uptime, and real-time data feeding automated journeys. Reporting should reach conversion and support holdout groups. It also matters whether SMS works within the same journeys and customer profile as your other channels, like email, in-app, web, and your paid media messaging.

[How much does SMS marketing cost?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/best-sms-marketing-platforms): SMS marketing cost depends on the platform, where you send, your number type, and volume. Most bills include a per-message cost, carrier fees, and one-time or annually recurring number registration fees. Longer texts, emojis, and MMS raise costs. Ask whether carrier fees are included in the quoted per-message cost, so you can compare quotes like for like.

[Do I need a separate platform for SMS and email?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/best-sms-marketing-platforms): No, and running them separately can cause problems. Separate tools can send duplicate messages, apply frequency caps to one channel only, create disjointed brand experiences, and struggle to show which channel drove a sale. A cross-channel platform runs SMS and email from one customer profile. A dedicated SMS tool still suits brands that only send texts.

[What compliance rules apply to SMS marketing in the US?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/best-sms-marketing-platforms): The TCPA, enforced by the FCC, sets the federal baseline for consent, opt-outs, and sending hours. Many states add stricter rules. CTIA guidelines cover opt-in disclosures and restricted content, and carriers enforce those alongside their own policies. Breaking the law risks fines, while carriers can filter or block your messages. This isn't legal advice. Check with your legal team.

[What is lead nurturing?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/lead-nurturing): Lead nurturing is the practice of building a relationship with someone who has shown interest but hasn't yet purchased, by sending a planned sequence of relevant messages that respond to their behavior until they buy or disengage.

[How is lead nurturing different for consumer brands than for B2B?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/lead-nurturing): The goal is the same in both, but the path differs. B2B nurture often supports a considered purchase made by several people, with lead scoring and a handoff to a sales rep. Consumer nurture usually follows one person, has no rep involved, runs on behavior across email, push, in-app messages, and SMS, and hands off at the first purchase.

[How long should a nurture journey be?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/lead-nurturing): A nurture journey should last as long as it takes each person to either buy or show they’re not ready. Behavior, instead of a fixed number of days, sets the length of the sequence. People showing intent move to the offer quickly, while people who stop engaging leave for a slower, lower-frequency path after a defined period.

[What is the difference between lead nurturing and a promotional campaign?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/lead-nurturing): A promotional campaign is built around an offer, such as a seasonal sale, and is usually scheduled by the business for a chosen segment. Lead nurturing is built around where each person is in their journey. Each person enters when they take an action, receives messages based on what they do, and leaves when they reach a defined outcome.

[When does lead nurturing end?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/lead-nurturing): Lead nurturing ends at the first purchase. That purchase should act as a defined trigger, removing the person from every nurture journey and moving them into retention programs at the same moment. People who never buy leave nurture through a different exit, moving to a lower-frequency path after a set period without engagement.

[What is a customer experience platform?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/customer-experience-platform): A customer experience platform is software that helps an organization observe, measure, and improve how customers experience it across every point of contact, from marketing and product through to service and support. It draws on survey and feedback data, contact center records, and behavioral signals to show how customers feel and why. It’s often a system of insight.

[What is the difference between a CX platform and a CEP?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/customer-experience-platform): A customer experience (CX) platform is often a system of insight, and a customer engagement platform (CEP) is a system of action. Experience management is largely about understanding and improving how customers feel about an organization, while engagement is about deciding and delivering what an individual customer receives next. One finds problems, and the other acts on them.

[Is a CX platform the same as CXM or CEM?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/customer-experience-platform): No. Customer experience (CX) is how customers perceive every interaction they have with an organization, across marketing, product, purchase, service, and support. Customer experience management (CXM, sometimes CEM) is the practice of collecting, measuring, and acting on that perception to improve it over time. A CX platform is the software that supports it.

[Do you need both a customer experience platform and a customer engagement platform?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/customer-experience-platform): Many organizations run both because they do different jobs. A customer experience platform is often a system of insight, showing where the experience falls short. A customer engagement platform is a system of action, deciding and delivering what each customer receives next. Which comes first depends on whether understanding or acting is the bigger need.

[What should you look for in customer experience software?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/customer-experience-platform): Look for software that collects survey, contact center, and service ticket data and joins it to a single customer record instead of reporting only in aggregate. Check whether it can trigger an action or only produce a report, who is expected to run it, how it handles consent and data residency, and what it costs to keep current.

[What is targeted email marketing?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/targeted-email-marketing): Targeted email marketing is the practice of deciding who receives an email based on what you know about them. That knowledge comes from consented, first-party data, such as what customers have bought, browsed, and opted into, so each campaign goes only to the people it’s relevant to instead of the whole list.

[What is the difference between targeted email marketing and email personalization?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/targeted-email-marketing): Targeting decides who receives an email, and personalization decides what that email contains. A targeted campaign might go only to customers who browsed running gear this month. Personalization then changes the subject line, products, or offer that each recipient sees. You can use either on its own, though most programs use both.

[How small should an email segment be?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/targeted-email-marketing): Small enough that everyone in it has a clear reason to get the message, and large enough to measure. There’s no fixed number. A few hundred people can be right for a high-value message, but if you want to compare results against a holdout group, both groups need enough people for the difference to mean something.

[Does sending fewer, more targeted emails reduce revenue?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/targeted-email-marketing): Sometimes, in the short term. Cutting broad sends removes some revenue from occasional buyers who wouldn’t qualify for a narrower audience. Over the following months, fewer unsubscribes and complaints and better inbox placement can raise revenue per recipient enough to recover the difference. A holdout group shows whether each send is adding revenue or just taking credit for it.

[Is buying an email list a form of targeting?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/targeted-email-marketing): No. A bought list is made up of people who never agreed to hear from you, so you have no consent to email them and no behavior to base targeting on. Sending to it also tends to drive up bounces and spam complaints, which damage sender reputation and push your emails toward spam for real customers too.

[What is funnel optimization?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/funnel-optimization): Funnel optimization is the practice of measuring how many people move from one stage of a funnel to the next, identifying the stage with the largest drop-off relative to what's achievable, and making changes at that stage to fix the issues and lift conversions.

[What is the difference between funnel optimization and conversion rate optimization?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/funnel-optimization): Conversion rate optimization focuses on improving a specific page or flow, such as a sign-up form or checkout, so more people complete it. Funnel optimization is broader. It looks across every stage of the funnel, including what happens between visits, to find where the most people are lost. The two are complementary and work best together.

[Which funnel stage should you optimize first?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/funnel-optimization): Start with the stage where the most people are lost relative to what’s achievable, based on your own history, segments, or past results. Then diagnose the cause at that stage before choosing a fix. The same drop-off rate can have different causes at different stages, and the wrong fix can make things worse.

[How do you know a funnel change worked?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/funnel-optimization): Compare the people who received the change with a holdout group who didn’t. Measure both on a fixed cohort, use an attribution window long enough to capture conversions that happen on a later visit, and state which denominator every rate uses. The difference between the two groups is the lift the change created.

[What is an engagement funnel?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/funnel-optimization): An engagement funnel tracks how people interact with a brand across the whole relationship, from awareness through conversion and on into retention and loyalty. Unlike a conversion funnel, which ends at a single action inside one visit, it follows the same customer from one visit to the next, including the time between them.

[What is relationship marketing?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/relationship-marketing): Relationship marketing is a strategy that treats each customer interaction as part of an ongoing relationship rather than an isolated transaction, using what a brand knows about a customer to earn attention over time instead of buying it repeatedly. In practice, it depends on knowing who each customer is, what they've agreed to receive, and what they've done before.

[What is the difference between relationship marketing and transactional marketing?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/relationship-marketing): Transactional marketing optimizes the next purchase and judges each campaign by what it sold. Relationship marketing optimizes the sequence of purchases and the cost of earning each one, using a customer's history and preferences to decide what to send and when. A brand can run both, with sales and launches alongside its lifecycle programs.

[What are examples of relationship marketing?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/relationship-marketing): Examples include newsletters that show offers based on a customer's membership status, renewal offers sent before a subscription lapses, personalized year-in-review experiences in an app, WhatsApp messages tailored to how recently someone last ordered, and SMS offers from the local store a customer actually uses, each based on that customer's own history.

[Is relationship marketing the same as CRM?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/relationship-marketing): No. A CRM is a system of record for accounts and contacts, typically built around sales and service workflows. Relationship marketing is a practice, the work of deciding what each customer hears and when. A consumer brand usually runs that practice from a customer engagement platform, which acts on customer data across channels.

[In email marketing, what is a relationship email?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/relationship-marketing): A relationship email updates a customer about an existing relationship with a brand, like a change to their account, membership, or subscription terms. Under the US CAN-SPAM Act, these "transactional or relationship" messages are mostly exempt from the rules for commercial email, provided they don't contain false or misleading routing information.

[How do you measure relationship marketing?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/relationship-marketing): Compare customers who receive a program with a random holdout group who don't, then track outcomes like retention, repeat purchase rate, and customer lifetime value over several months. Opens and clicks show early engagement, but the holdout comparison shows what the program actually added beyond what customers would have done anyway.

[What is customer journey optimization?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/customer-journey-optimization): Customer journey optimization is the practice of measuring how customers move through a journey, finding the points where they stall or leave, and changing the timing, channel, message, or offer at those points to improve the outcome. Each change is treated as a test, measured against outcomes such as conversion, retention, or satisfaction.

[How is customer journey optimization different from customer journey automation?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/customer-journey-optimization): Customer journey automation is how you build and run a journey; customer journey optimization improves it after it’s live. Automation uses triggers and predefined workflows to send messages or take actions without manual effort, such as a reminder after an abandoned cart. Optimization measures how an automated customer journey performs and changes what isn't performing.

[What metrics show that a customer journey needs optimizing?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/customer-journey-optimization): The clearest signs are high drop-off at a specific stage or step, falling conversion rates between stages, and a lengthening time to convert. Rising churn, fewer repeat purchases, and declining satisfaction or effort scores also point to friction. Track each stage separately, because a single overall conversion rate shows that a problem exists but not where customers leave.

[How often should a customer journey be reviewed?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/customer-journey-optimization): Review each core journey at least quarterly, and check a change at day 7, day 30, and day 90 as each cohort reaches those points. Review sooner when something significant changes, such as a new product, price, channel, or market. Monitor conversion and drop-off continuously so problems show up between reviews.

[Do you need a separate tool to optimize a customer journey?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/customer-journey-optimization): Not necessarily, but you do need two distinct layers. Journey analytics measures how customers move across channels and shows where they stall or leave. A customer engagement platform acts on those findings by changing the timing, channel, message, or offer customers receive. Some platforms combine both, while others focus on one layer and connect to the other.

[What are examples of email marketing?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/email-marketing-examples): Email marketing examples are real campaigns that show what a brand sent, why it sent it, and what happened next, from a welcome message to a win-back offer. Common examples include a welcome series for new subscribers, a reminder after a shopper abandons a cart, a replenishment email when a product runs low, and an offer for a lapsed customer.

[What are the most common types of marketing emails?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/email-marketing-examples): The most common types of marketing emails are welcome, promotional, transactional, lifecycle and triggered, newsletter and content, and re-engagement emails. Transactional emails confirm something the customer did, such as placing an order, while promotional emails are scheduled by the brand. Triggered emails respond to behavior like browsing, and re-engagement emails go to customers who have gone quiet.

[What makes an email marketing campaign effective?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/email-marketing-examples): An effective email marketing campaign is triggered by something the customer did, gives each email one job, and changes its content for each recipient. It also works as one step in a sequence alongside other channels, and it goes only to people who opted in, which keeps the list healthy and helps ensure that emails reach the customer’s inbox.

[What are examples of personalized marketing emails?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/email-marketing-examples): Personalized marketing emails include a browse abandonment email showing the exact product someone viewed, a weekly email of recommendations based on purchase history, and a newsletter whose offers change with each reader's membership status. Personalization can also cover timing, with each email sent at the hour that person is most likely to open it.

[How do brands use email alongside SMS and push in a sequence?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/email-marketing-examples): Brands use email as one step in a cross-channel sequence, where each message depends on what the customer did after the last one. A cart reminder, for example, might start as an in-app message, move to email a few hours later, and reach SMS only if both go unopened, stopping on every channel once the customer checks out.

[What is conversational commerce?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/conversational-commerce): Conversational commerce is buying, selling, and customer service carried out inside a two-way conversation on messaging apps, text, in-app chat, or voice, where the shopper can ask, decide, and complete a purchase or a service request without leaving the thread.

[What are examples of conversational commerce?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/conversational-commerce): A shopper texting to reorder a product in a new size, with an AI agent confirming the size and placing the order by text, is one example. Others include asking a fashion retailer on WhatsApp whether a dress is in stock and making the payment from within the chat, or moving a grocery delivery slot through in-app chat.

[What is the difference between conversational commerce and conversational marketing?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/conversational-commerce): Conversational marketing starts and nurtures the conversation, and conversational commerce completes the transaction inside it. Conversational marketing uses two-way dialogue to engage shoppers and build interest. Conversational commerce takes over when the shopper is ready to act, letting them buy, reorder, or sort out a service request without leaving the conversation.

[Which channels are used for conversational commerce?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/conversational-commerce): The main channels are WhatsApp, SMS and RCS, in-app and web messaging, social commerce and marketplace chat, and voice assistants. WhatsApp, SMS, RCS, and in-app are owned channels, where the brand manages consent and keeps the conversation data. Social and marketplace chat add reach, but the platform owns those conversations.

[What does a conversational commerce platform need to do?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/conversational-commerce): A conversational commerce platform needs to cover owned messaging channels with built-in consent management, share one customer profile with email and push, and connect to catalog and order systems. It should also support AI agents that work within guardrails and hand off to a person, and measure conversation-assisted conversion against a baseline.

[What is conversational AI in eCommerce?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/conversational-ai-ecommerce): Conversational AI in eCommerce is software that understands natural-language messages from shoppers and responds, recommends, or completes a task in a two-way conversation, across the messaging channels a brand owns. It relies on connection to real customer profile and catalog data, and knows when to hand off to a person.

[How is conversational AI used in retail and eCommerce?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/conversational-ai-ecommerce): Across the whole buyer journey. Before purchase, shoppers describe what they want and get relevant options back. At purchase, sizing and stock questions are answered. After purchase, order status and reorders, delivery changes, and returns run through the same conversational thread.

[What is the difference between conversational AI and a chatbot?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/conversational-ai-ecommerce): The difference is in architecture. A scripted bot matches messages against keywords it already knows and follows a pre-scripted decision tree. Conversational AI interprets intent from free text, retains information across an entire conversation, and can act on what it finds, including checking stock, placing an order, or changing a delivery.

[Which messaging channels work for conversational AI in eCommerce?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/conversational-ai-ecommerce): Any channel supporting a two-way exchange. WhatsApp Business messaging carries the richest conversations, SMS reaches almost anyone with a phone, RCS adds branded formatting with SMS fallback, and in-app messaging brings signed-in context. Owned channels have the advantage that conversations write back to your own customer profiles.

[How do eCommerce brands measure conversational AI?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/conversational-ai-ecommerce): By resolution and revenue, not deflection. Track how many conversations reached a resolution, how many assisted a conversion, and the effect on repurchase rate. Deflection shows how much work the agent absorbed, not what it earned. To isolate the agent's impact, compare these figures against a control group or the journey it replaced.

[Can conversational AI take orders or reorders over SMS or WhatsApp?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/conversational-ai-ecommerce): Yes. An agent connected to your catalog and order system can confirm a product, place an order, and process a change inside the message thread, with no website visit. Braze customer Aeroflow Health's agents handle SMS reorders this way, interpreting requests like "next size up" and matching them to the catalog. Repurchase conversions rose 8.8% compared with its previous SMS journey.

[What is marketing automation?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/marketing-automation): Marketing automation is software that sends marketing messages and runs marketing tasks automatically, based on rules and customer behavior, across channels such as email, push, SMS, in-app, and web, so each customer gets the right message without a person sending it. Each program combines a trigger, a decision, and an action, then keeps running as customers act.

[What is the difference between marketing automation and a customer engagement platform?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/marketing-automation): An email service provider runs one channel, a marketing automation platform runs rules and journeys, and a customer engagement platform unifies customer data into one profile and coordinates messages across channels from it. Marketing automation platforms grew out of lead management, and customer engagement platforms are designed for consumer brands reaching large audiences across several channels.

[What is B2C marketing automation?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/marketing-automation): B2C marketing automation applies automation to consumer relationships, with each program acting on one customer's behavior at a time. Journeys start from behavioral events such as sessions, purchases, and lapses, and reach customers through push, SMS, in-app, and WhatsApp as readily as email. The goal is to grow customer lifetime value across the entire relationship.

[What does enterprise marketing automation require?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/marketing-automation): Enterprise marketing automation requires a platform that can ingest high volumes of events, resolve identity across app, web, and store, and enforce governance through roles, approvals, and brand guardrails. It also needs consent management that handles regional rules, experimentation with control groups, and AI that selects messages for one customer at a time.

[How does AI change marketing automation?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/marketing-automation): AI changes marketing automation in two ways. Generative AI drafts the content variants that automation needs in volume, and marketers review and approve them. AI-driven selection chooses the message, channel, and timing for each customer based on observed outcomes, working within rules such as eligibility and frequency limits.

[How do you measure personalized marketing?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/personalized-marketing): How do you measure personalized marketing? Hold back a randomized control group from the personalized experience and compare it against the group that receives it. The difference is lift, and it separates the effect of personalization from seasonality, pricing changes, or other campaigns running at the same time. Track it alongside conversion, retention, and revenue per recipient.

[What are the biggest barriers to personalized marketing?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/personalized-marketing): The biggest barriers are fragmented data, stale profiles, and personalization that stops at one channel. When email, push, and SMS read from different records, customers get contradictory messages. Teams also run out of time to write and maintain rules for every segment, which is why many move from manual rules to AI-driven selection as volume grows.

[What is omnichannel commerce?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/omnichannel-commerce): Omnichannel commerce is a way of running a retail business so customers can shop, pay, collect, return, and get help across your store, website, app, and messaging as one continuous experience, with the same cart, inventory view, and customer record behind every touchpoint. It depends on four shared elements: customer identity, inventory, the cart and order, and the conversation.

[What is the difference between omnichannel commerce and omnichannel marketing?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/omnichannel-commerce): Omnichannel marketing covers how a brand communicates across channels, while omnichannel commerce covers how it sells, fulfills, and serves across them. Marketing coordinates messages, offers, and timing. Commerce connects the cart, inventory, orders, pickups, and returns. Both draw on the same customer profile, so what a shopper buys in one channel shapes what they hear in the next.

[What is the difference between omnichannel and unified commerce?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/omnichannel-commerce): Unified commerce is one way to deliver omnichannel commerce. Omnichannel commerce describes the connected experience a customer gets across store, web, app, and messaging. Unified commerce describes running that experience on one commerce backbone, with catalog, inventory, orders, and customer records in a single system instead of separate systems connected together.

[What does an omnichannel commerce platform do?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/omnichannel-commerce): An omnichannel commerce platform usually runs the commerce layer: the catalog, pricing, cart, and checkout that every storefront uses. It's one of five layers in the stack, alongside order management, point of sale, customer data, and engagement. No single product covers all five for an enterprise brand, so the platform has to share data with the other layers.

[How do brands measure omnichannel commerce?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/omnichannel-commerce): Brands measure omnichannel commerce by outcomes across channels, such as repeat purchase rate, pickup completion, and repurchase after a return. To see what their engagement program caused, they hold back a control group that receives no messages and compare its behavior with shoppers who did.

[Which channels does Content Optimizer support, and how many combinations can I test?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/content-optimizer-product-spotlight): Content Optimizer works across email, push, and SMS/MMS and RCS. You can test up to 625 combinations in email, 125 in SMS, RCS, and MMS, and 25 in push.

[Do I have to use AI-generated variants?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/content-optimizer-product-spotlight): No. You can write every variant yourself, ask BrazeAIᵀᴹ to suggest variants from your seed copy, or mix both. You choose which variants go into the step.

[How does Content Optimizer decide what to send?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/content-optimizer-product-spotlight): When the step first launches, it sends combinations randomly to collect performance data. From there, a multi-armed bandit algorithm shifts more sends toward combinations that perform well on the event you chose, such as opens or clicks for email, and fewer toward the ones that don't. Each person receives one message per entry into the step.

[How much volume do I need?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/content-optimizer-product-spotlight): Content Optimizer works best in always-on Canvases where users enter gradually, with at least a few thousand users per day. If everyone enters at once, the algorithm has no time to learn from early results.

[How is Content Optimizer different from A/B testing?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/content-optimizer-product-spotlight): A classic A/B test compares a small number of variants on an even split until you pick a winner. Content Optimizer tests many combinations of elements together, moves traffic toward winners while the test runs, and keeps adjusting for as long as the Canvas is live.

[Does it personalize for each individual customer?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/content-optimizer-product-spotlight): No. Content Optimizer finds the best-performing combination for your audience as a whole. For per-recipient decisions, look at BrazeAI Decisioning Studioᵀᴹ.

[Does it work with quiet hours and Intelligent Timing?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/content-optimizer-product-spotlight): Yes. Content Optimizer behaves like the Message step in Canvas, with features like quiet hours, Intelligent Timing, and event logging.

[Can I use it for multiple languages?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/content-optimizer-product-spotlight): Not within a single step. Multi-language settings aren't supported in Content Optimizer steps, so use one step per language and branch your paths.

[What is the difference between Braze and Iterable?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/braze-vs-iterable-comparison): Both orchestrate messaging across email, push, SMS and in-app from a unified customer profile. Braze started as a mobile SDK in 2011, so its in-product messaging runs deeper and segments update in real time as data arrives. Iterable started with email, and email maturity is a genuine strength of its platform — but that email-first architecture also means more of its data movement runs on a schedule rather than natively in real time.

[Is Braze or Iterable better for email marketing?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/braze-vs-iterable-comparison): Iterable offers more flexibility on infrastructure — it connects to email service provider accounts you already own, so an existing sender reputation comes with you, and a dedicated IP is available above 150,000 messages a month. That flexibility comes with a trade-off: you're responsible for managing that ESP relationship, running your own IP warm-up, and coordinating with a separate provider if deliverability issues come up. Braze sends email natively as one channel among many, with documented throughput of up to roughly 115 million messages an hour across 32 IPs, so reputation and infrastructure are managed inside the platform rather than split across vendors.

[How do Braze and Iterable handle data from a warehouse?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/braze-vs-iterable-comparison): Braze Cloud Data Ingestion connects to Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, Redshift, Azure and S3, with zero-copy segmentation building audiences without copying data in — all native to the platform. Iterable Smart Ingest supports 23 or more sources and is configured through a no-code interface, but it's co-developed with Hightouch, a third-party reverse-ETL provider, syncs on a 15-minute floor, and includes only five free production syncs per organization each month before scaling further requires a separate commercial relationship with Hightouch. If something breaks, that's two vendors to coordinate with instead of one.

[What channels do Braze and Iterable support?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/braze-vs-iterable-comparison): Braze covers email, push, SMS, MMS, RCS, WhatsApp, KakaoTalk, LINE, in-app messages, banners, Content Cards, landing pages, webhooks and audience sync. Iterable covers email, mobile push, in-app, SMS, web push, social and direct mail, coordinated through Studio.

[How long does it take to migrate from Iterable to Braze?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/braze-vs-iterable-comparison): Published migrations range from a few weeks to several months. Timing depends on how clean your event data is, how many templates need rebuilding, and whether engineering time is allocated to the project or borrowed from another.

[What is the closest alternative to Iterable?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/iterable-alternatives): Braze, on the evidence of third-party reviewers. G2 ranks it first of ten Iterable alternatives and names it the best overall. It matches Iterable most closely on cross-channel orchestration and mobile depth.

[What are the best Iterable alternatives for enterprise teams?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/iterable-alternatives): Braze, Salesforce Marketing Cloud Engagement, and Adobe Journey Optimizer. Braze suits enterprises whose journeys react to behavior as it happens across app, web, and messaging. Salesforce suits large organizations with the IT resourcing to run a multi-product footprint, and publishes pricing. Adobe suits teams already committed to its wider platform, and is the only option here whose templating language matches Iterable's.

[What are the best Iterable alternatives for startups?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/iterable-alternatives): Klaviyo and Customer.io. Klaviyo publishes its pricing and is free up to 250 active profiles, which suits e-commerce teams beginning with email and SMS. Customer.io publishes tier prices and overage rates, and includes every messaging channel on its entry plan, suiting product-led teams comfortable working with event data.

[Why do companies switch away from Iterable?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/iterable-alternatives): Streaming segmentation and analytics limits come up most. Dynamic lists refresh at send time rather than continuously, and scheduled lists recalculate once a day. Holdouts sit inside individual experiments rather than across a whole program, and no report shows drop-off across a sequence of events you define.

[How long does it take to migrate from Iterable to a new platform?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/iterable-alternatives): It depends on channel count, program size, and how much template rework is needed. Email is usually the constraint, since IP warm-up runs over several weeks before full volume can move. Both platforms typically run in parallel through that period. Ask each vendor to quote a timeline for a program your size.

[How long does it take to implement Braze?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/braze-implementation-guide-startups): How long a Braze implementation takes for a startup depends on preparation quality and engineering availability, not a fixed schedule. Teams with clean customer data and one clear use case can generally move quickly, since the technical track runs on engineering sprint cycles while the marketing track builds in parallel rather than waiting for full sign-off.

[How do startups prepare for a Braze implementation?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/braze-implementation-guide-startups): Startups prepare for a Braze implementation by defining a primary KPI, mapping where their customer data lives, and choosing one first use case instead of launching everything at once. They also assign clear owners for SDK integration and campaign building, and ready creative templates before the first journey goes live.

[What do you need before starting a Braze implementation?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/braze-implementation-guide-startups): Before starting a Braze implementation you need a defined goal and primary KPI, a clear picture of your customer data and its sources, a chosen first use case, and named owners for the technical and marketing work. Having creative and messaging templates ready helps keeping the first launch from stalling.

[Is Braze hard to set up for a small team?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/braze-implementation-guide-startups): Braze is not hard to set up for a small team. It's a marketer-operated platform, so once the data layer is partially live, a marketer can build segments, journeys, and templates without constant engineering support. Lean teams often launch faster than large organizations working through legacy systems and approvals.

[How quickly can a startup launch its first campaign in Braze?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/braze-implementation-guide-startups): A startup can expect to see early results within weeks of launching its first journey, provided the data is ready and one use case is in focus. Pazza Pasta got up and running in two days and drove higher purchase rates on WhatsApp than email, which shows a contained first launch can produce measurable results soon after going live.

[What's the main difference between Braze and Adobe Experience Cloud?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/braze-vs-adobe-comparison): The main difference between Braze and Adobe Experience Cloud is scope. Braze focuses on real-time customer engagement and lifecycle messaging across channels like push, in-app, email, and SMS, while Adobe Experience Cloud is a broader suite that connects engagement with tools for data, content, analytics, and governance.

[Is Braze or Adobe better for mobile marketing?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/braze-vs-adobe-comparison): Whether Braze or Adobe is better for mobile marketing depends on how central push and in-app are to your customer experience. Braze is commonly evaluated when mobile messaging is a primary channel, while Adobe’s mobile capabilities vary based on the products in your deployment.

[How do Braze and Adobe compare on ease of use and implementation time?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/braze-vs-adobe-comparison): How Braze and Adobe compare on ease of use and implementation time depends on rollout scope and team structure. Braze is often implemented as an engagement layer connected to existing data sources, while Adobe implementations can involve more products, stakeholders, and governance steps.

[Can I use Braze with Adobe tools?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/braze-vs-adobe-comparison): Yes, you can use Braze with Adobe tools. Many teams use Adobe for parts of their experience stack and use Braze to run real-time customer engagement, with clear data flows, identity matching, and consent and preference management across both.

[Is Braze or Adobe better for real-time personalization?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/braze-vs-adobe-comparison): Whether Braze or Adobe is better for real-time personalization depends on where personalization needs to happen and how quickly it needs to adapt. Braze is designed to respond to customer behavior across lifecycle channels, while Adobe’s capabilities vary by product mix and how your data and orchestration are set up.

[How do Braze and Adobe compare on pricing?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/braze-vs-adobe-comparison): How Braze and Adobe compare on pricing starts with what drives cost. Braze uses a value-based pricing model based on Platform Editions, Monthly Active Users (MAU), and Flexible Credits, while Adobe pricing varies based on product packaging, implementation scope, and services, so total cost of ownership depends on your deployment and resourcing model.

[What are examples of SMS marketing?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/sms-marketing-examples): SMS marketing examples include order and delivery updates, limited-time offers, abandoned cart reminders, back-in-stock alerts, loyalty rewards, two-way messaging, and win-back campaigns. Most sit inside a wider cross-channel journey.

[What are the best SMS marketing use cases for B2C brands?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/sms-marketing-examples): The best SMS marketing use cases for B2C brands are time-sensitive moments where immediacy matters, such as delivery updates, abandoned carts, limited-time offers, and reorder reminders. The right mix depends on the business.

[How often should a brand send marketing texts?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/sms-marketing-examples): There's no single right frequency. It depends on how often customers buy, how time-sensitive the messages are, and what customers were told about frequency when they opted in. A restaurant with weekly deals may suit more frequent texts than a travel brand. A rising opt-out rate is an early sign of sending too often.

[What is the difference between SMS and RCS marketing?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/sms-marketing-examples): SMS marketing sends plain text messages, while RCS marketing adds verified, branded sending, rich media such as images and video, carousels, suggested replies and actions, and read analytics. RCS depends on carrier and device support, which varies by country, so brands use SMS fallback for messages that can't be delivered as RCS.

[Do customers have to opt in to marketing texts?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/sms-marketing-examples): Yes, generally. In the U.S., marketing texts require the customer's prior express written consent, meaning a clear agreement to receive marketing messages at that number. Customers can also opt out at any time, including by replying STOP. Rules differ by country, and some allow limited exceptions, so check with legal counsel.

[What can you do with the BrazeAI Operatorᵀᴹ?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/brazeai-operator-use-cases): Operator drafts campaigns, Canvases, segments, messages, and Content Blocks from plain-language prompts. It writes and explains Liquid, builds agents in BrazeAI Agent Console™, reviews content before you send, and creates reports and dashboards. It also answers "how do I" questions about Braze in the context of the page you're working on.

[How fast can you build a campaign with BrazeAI Operatorᵀᴹ?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/brazeai-operator-use-cases): Timings depend on complexity, but the pattern is consistent: Describe the campaign in a prompt, review what Operator drafts, and refine it without filing an engineering ticket. For example, Virgin Media O2 brought campaign build iterations down from two full days to roughly 15 minutes after adopting Catalogs with Operator's help.

[Does BrazeAI Operatorᵀᴹ act autonomously, or require human approval?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/brazeai-operator-use-cases): It requires approval by default. Operator will propose a plan or suggested steps to take, and then shows each change as an action card to approve or decline. Teams can turn on auto-approve to skip that step, though generating images and changing workspace settings always need explicit approval.

[Can marketers use Braze without developer support day to day?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/brazeai-operator-use-cases): Yes. Day-to-day self-sufficiency is the norm once the data layer is live. Engineering handles the one-time technical work of onboarding onto the Braze platform, including SDK integration, data ingestion, identity strategy, event and attribute modeling. Once data is flowing, marketers build campaigns, segments, journeys, and reports themselves, with Operator writing the Liquid and SQL that previously needed a specialist or a place in a sprint queue.

[How does Braze connect to a data warehouse?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/brazeai-operator-use-cases): Cloud Data Ingestion connects Braze directly to Snowflake, Redshift, BigQuery, Databricks, and Microsoft Fabric. It syncs user attributes, events, and catalog data on a schedule you set, so personalization runs from the data you already hold rather than requiring a separate pipeline built and maintained by your engineering team.

[How can B2C brands deliver 1:1 personalization at scale?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/b2c-personalization): Brands deliver 1:1 personalization at scale by unifying customer profiles, using AI decisioning to choose the best message, channel, and timing per person, and orchestrating cross-channel journeys with guardrails like frequency caps. AI agents and reusable content make individual-level relevance possible across millions of consumers.

[How can B2C marketers personalize web experiences?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/b2c-personalization): Marketers personalize web experiences by using real-time behavioral data — pages viewed, products browsed, session activity — to tailor on-site messages, banners, and recommendations. Web personalization works best when connected to the same unified profile powering email, push, and in-app, so the experience stays consistent across channels.

[What are examples of successful B2C personalization programs?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/b2c-personalization): Successful programs include retailers turning friction points like out-of-stock items into personalized re-engagement, streaming services sending individualized content recommendations that reduce churn, and financial services brands guiding customers through onboarding and key money moments. The common thread: real-time data, one unified profile, and cross-channel delivery.

[How do you balance privacy and personalization in B2C marketing?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/b2c-personalization): Balance privacy and personalization by collecting only the data you need, being transparent about why, and honoring consent per channel. Prioritize zero-party and first-party data customers share willingly, offer a preference center, and base messages on recent actions people would expect you to use.

[How do you personalize product recommendations?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/b2c-personalization): Personalize product recommendations by ranking items on each customer's behavior, affinity, and context — recent browsing, past purchases, and availability. AI-powered recommendations update in real time and render dynamically across email, push, in-app, and web, so every customer sees the most relevant products in the moment.

[What is the best email marketing platform in 2027?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/best-email-marketing-platforms): There isn't one. The right platform depends on how much you send, how deeply you personalize, how much deliverability control you need and how much of the program runs automatically. Klaviyo suits ecommerce, Mailchimp suits small businesses, HubSpot suits CRM-led teams, and Braze suits consumer brands sending real-time, personalized email at volume.

[What features should an email marketing platform include?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/best-email-marketing-platforms): A drag-and-drop builder with reusable content blocks, audience segmentation across behavioral and transactional data, triggered sending that fires on customer actions, deliverability infrastructure covering dedicated IPs, IP warming and inbox placement monitoring. Look for AI that aids your email marketing workflow (whether that’s content generation or decisioning), data warehouse integrations, and flexible reporting that ties sends to revenue.

[Is Braze an email marketing platform?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/best-email-marketing-platforms): Yes, Braze is an email marketing platform. It sends hundreds of billions of emails a year, with a drag-and-drop and HTML editor, Figma and Canva integrations, real-time behavioral triggers, personalization at send or open, automated IP warming and an in-house deliverability team. Other channels are available but not required.

[What is the difference between an email service provider (ESP) and a customer engagement platform?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/best-email-marketing-platforms): An email service provider (ESP) handles email only: lists, templates, automation and deliverability. A customer engagement platform runs email alongside push, SMS, in-app and web from one customer profile, coordinating between them. Both send email well. The difference is whether other channels are available later without moving to a different system.

[How much does an email marketing platform cost?](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/best-email-marketing-platforms): Cost depends on the features you need and how many active users or contacts. Some platforms have free or trial tiers. For enterprise packages, you usually need to ask for a custom quote.
